candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'Wisdom found no place where she might dwell; then a dwelling-place was assigned her in the heavens. Wisdom went forth to make her dwelling among the children of men, and found no dwelling-place' — the failed earthly mission of Wisdom. Tewahedo Christology reads this verse Christologically (after Pr 8:22-31, Wisd 7:25-26) as anticipating the Incarnation's reversal: the Word/Wisdom who could find no place on earth in the Parables ultimately does find a place — in Mary's womb.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'Then Wisdom returned to her place, and took her seat among the angels. And iniquity went forth from her chambers: whom she sought not she found, and dwelt with them, as rain in a desert and dew on a thirsty land' — Wisdom's withdrawal contrasted with iniquity's flourishing. Tewahedo monastic qǝne (sacred poetry) preserves this image as the canonical illustration of why Christ's coming was necessary: Wisdom alone could not stay; she required incarnation. The verse is cited in Tewahedo Marian liturgy as the antecedent that Mary's fiat reverses.
